body_es: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall), AWS Shield y otros servicios conforman la defensa perimetral de aplicaciones en AWS. AWS WAF protege aplicaciones web de exploits comunes: inyección SQL, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), ataques de bot, y vulnerabilidades del OWASP Top 10. Se despliega delante de CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway o AppSync mediante Web ACLs que contienen reglas. Las Managed Rule Groups de AWS y del AWS Marketplace permiten protección inmediata sin escribir reglas manualmente. Las Custom Rules pueden filtrar por IP, país, cabeceras HTTP, cadena de consulta, o body. El rate limiting bloquea IPs que superen un número de solicitudes por 5 minutos. AWS Shield Standard está incluido de forma gratuita para todos los clientes de AWS y protege automáticamente contra ataques DDoS de red y transporte (Capa 3/4). AWS Shield Advanced (3.000 USD/mes) añade protección contra ataques sofisticados de Capa 7, acceso 24/7 al equipo AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT), protección de costos durante ataques, y visibilidad avanzada mediante CloudWatch. Para el SAA-C03, la arquitectura de defensa en capas es: Route 53 (DNS con anycast routing) + CloudFront + AWS Shield + AWS WAF + ACM (HTTPS) + Security Groups y NACLs. Amazon GuardDuty detecta amenazas mediante análisis de logs (VPC Flow Logs, CloudTrail, DNS), mientras AWS Inspector evalúa vulnerabilidades en instancias EC2 y contenedores.
body_en: AWS WAF, AWS Shield, and related services form the perimeter security layer for internet-facing AWS workloads. AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) operates at Layer 7 and protects against OWASP Top 10 exploits including SQL injection, XSS, and malicious bots. It deploys in front of CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, or AppSync via Web ACLs containing ordered rule groups. AWS Managed Rule Groups provide immediate coverage for known threat categories without manual rule authoring. Custom Rules filter on IP sets, geographic origin, HTTP headers, query strings, request body content, and rate limits. Rate-based rules automatically block IP addresses that exceed a configured request threshold within five minutes. AWS Shield Standard is automatically active for all AWS customers at no additional cost, defending against volumetric and protocol-based DDoS attacks at Layers 3 and 4. AWS Shield Advanced ($3,000/month) adds protection against sophisticated Layer 7 attacks, 24/7 access to the AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT), cost protection for scaling during attacks, and real-time attack metrics in CloudWatch. For SAA-C03 exam scenarios, the layered defense architecture is: Route 53 + CloudFront + Shield + WAF + ACM for TLS + Security Groups. Amazon GuardDuty uses ML to detect threats in VPC Flow Logs, CloudTrail events, and DNS logs. AWS Inspector continuously scans EC2 instances and container images for software vulnerabilities and network exposure.
example_code:
# Create WAF ACL
aws wafv2 create-web-acl \
  --name my-acl \
  --scope REGIONAL \
  --default-action Block={} \
  --rules file://rules.json

# Attach to ALB
aws wafv2 associate-web-acl \
  --web-acl-arn arn:aws:wafv2:us-east-1:123456789012:regional/webacl/my-acl/abc123 \
  --resource-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456789012:loadbalancer/app/my-alb/1234567890abcdef
